questions.q: What is the dot product of u = (2, 3) and v = (4, -1)?
questions.explain: The dot product sums the products of corresponding entries: 2*4 + 3*(-1) = 8 - 3 = 5.

questions.q: What does it mean to say a matrix A represents a linear map?
options: A(c1*x + c2*y) = c1*A*x + c2*A*y for any scalars c1, c2 and vectors x, y
A must be a square matrix
A can only have positive entries
questions.explain: A linear map respects addition and scalar multiplication exactly as stated; this is the defining property, independent of whether A is square or invertible.

questions.q: For matrices A (size m x n) and B (size n x p), what are the dimensions of the product C = AB?
options: The product is undefined unless m = p
questions.explain: Matrix multiplication requires the inner dimensions to match (A's columns = B's rows, both n), and the result takes the outer dimensions: m x p.

questions.q: Which statement about matrix multiplication is true in general?
options: Matrix multiplication is associative, (AB)C = A(BC), but not commutative in general
Matrix multiplication is commutative but not associative
Matrix multiplication is undefined for square matrices
questions.explain: Matrix multiplication is associative but generally not commutative — AB and BA can differ even when both products are defined.

questions.q: In the factor-model example, asset_returns = B @ factor_returns where B is a 4x3 loading matrix, what does this computation represent?
options: A dot product producing a single scalar
A matrix-vector multiplication mapping 3 factor returns into 4 asset returns
An elementwise multiplication of two equal-length vectors
The inverse of the factor return vector
questions.explain: B is 4x3 and factor_returns has length 3, so B @ factor_returns is a matrix-vector multiplication producing a length-4 vector of asset returns — the linear map applied to the factor vector.
